payload.question: Is one retargeted checkpoint equivalent to per-target training, or is the null result simply underpowered?

difference_tests.wilcoxon_interpretation: at n = 7 the smallest attainable two-sided p is 2/2^7 = 0.015625 under any data; a large p here reflects the test's resolution at this sample size as much as the data, which is why the equivalence claim rests on the TOST rather than on this p-value

equivalence.margin_definition: mean within-target seed sd of the retargeted arm; a difference below the method's own reproducibility is not actionable
equivalence.decision_rule: pre-registered: claim equivalence only if TOST p < 0.05 at the margin AND still p < 0.05 at a 0.10 margin

payload.verdict: Equivalence established at a margin of 0.189 g/cm^3 (TOST p = 0.0023). The 95% CI on the paired difference is [-0.111, 0.086], so the claim is a bounded equivalence rather than an unrejected null. The design could have detected 0.135 g/cm^3 at 80% power, which is 20% of the per-target arm's own mean error. The pre-registered second condition is met: equivalence survives at a 0.10 margin (p = 0.0362), so the conclusion is not an artifact of the margin. The Wilcoxon result is p = 1.0 against a floor of 0.015625 attainable at n = 7, which is why it is not the basis of the claim.
